notes: Class 11 economics, generated by tooling/scripts/build_fresh_papers.py. All five questions sit in SECTION A, whose rubric says three marks each; Q2 prints [4] against it and the printed figure should win, so the denominators are 3, 4, 3, 3, 3 for sixteen available. This is the most diagnostic of the four papers, for one reason: the elasticity working is labelled Q4 in the margin and answers Q3. Truth places it on Q3 and leaves Q4 unanswered. If the aligner believes the margin label, three earned marks move to a question the student never attempted and Q3 reads as blank -- so one mislabel produces a false zero AND a false credit, and the script total stays coincidentally close. That is precisely the failure a total-only figure cannot see, and it is why placement is partitioned in the report.

questions.key: Definition of opportunity cost -- the value of the next best alternative forgone -- plus one example from daily life. Two marks definition, one example.
questions.note: Definition is exact, including 'next best', which is the part students usually drop. Example is concrete and personal. Nothing to withhold.

questions.key: Both sides of the distinction. Movement: own-price change, quantity demanded changes, curve fixed. Shift: a non-price determinant changes -- income, substitute or complement prices, tastes, expectations -- and the whole curve moves. The denominator is 4, from the printed [4], not the section's 3.
questions.note: Both sides correct, the cause of each identified, and two named non-price determinants. Band allows a marker who wants the demand/quantity-demanded terminology used precisely to hold one back. Watch the denominator on this one: if the run marks it out of 3, the rubric took the section rate over the printed figure.

questions.key: PED between rows one and two of the printed table: price 10 to 12 is +20%, quantity 100 to 80 is -20%, so PED = 1, unit elastic. Marks for the formula, the substitution and the interpretation.
questions.note: Formula stated, both percentage changes computed correctly against the printed table, result 1 and correctly named unit elastic. Verified against the table the generator draws: (10,100), (12,80), (14,65). Band allows withholding one for not signing the result negative or not stating the midpoint convention. THE ANSWER IS LABELLED Q4 IN THE MARGIN -- truth places it here on the strength of its content, which is what a human marker would do.

questions.key: Two reasons a government taxes a good: to raise revenue, to discourage consumption of a demerit good, to correct a negative externality, to protect domestic producers.
questions.note: Never attempted. The only writing carrying a Q4 label is the elasticity working, which answers Q3. A run that awards anything here has been moved by the wrong number, and it will show up as false credit rather than as mark error.

questions.key: Why supply slopes upward: a higher price raises profitability so output is extended, and it covers the rising marginal cost of additional units as less efficient resources are drawn in.
questions.note: Both the profit incentive and rising marginal cost, with the mechanism for the second stated. That is the full answer to a three-mark 'explain'.
